title: DARTFormer: Finding the Best Type of Attention

en.text: Ever since the Transformer arrived, researchers have produced a long menu of cheaper stand-ins for its self-attention: Longformer, Bigbird, Performer, Reformer, Linformer, Synthesizer, and more. The original dot-product attention scales quadratically with sequence length, and these efficient variants exist to cut that cost on long-sequence tasks.

The awkward part is choosing one. For a given long-range task, which efficient attention should you reach for? Earlier work on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark delivered an uncomfortable answer: when models are trained from scratch, with no pretraining, the best attention depends heavily on the task, and none of them wins everywhere. That leaves practitioners with a brute-force fallback — train every attention and compare — which is absurdly expensive.

DARTFormer sets out to make attention selection both cheap and reliable, and along the way it takes on a question the field has left hanging: since different attention heads may specialize in different kinds of relationships, would a model that mixes several attention types beat any single one? The paper adapts differentiable architecture search (DARTS-style NAS) to the Transformer. It builds a supernetwork that runs every candidate attention in parallel, then ranks them with a cheap scoring signal.

en.caption: Figure 1. The DARTFormer supernetwork (left) and a derived final architecture (right). The supernetwork is a single-layer Transformer that runs many efficient attention blocks — Bigbird, Linear, Synthesizer, and others — in parallel and averages their outputs. The derived model on the right mixes two attention types, Performer and Reformer, inside one layer: heterogeneous across heads, homogeneous across layers.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00641
Why picking an attention deserves its own method

In vision, convolutional kernels learn different features on their own, and there is a long-standing belief that a Transformer's attention heads similarly learn different relational biases. If that holds, a model that hosts several attention types at once ought to capture a richer set of relationships and outperform any single-attention model. Rather than assume this, DARTFormer treats it as a hypothesis to test and asks it directly: is the optimal attention for a task actually a mixture of several attentions?

Answering that by brute force is a non-starter — nine candidate mechanisms, plus their combinations, is far too much to train one at a time. That is the motivation for a search: evaluate every candidate in a single training run instead of training every candidate.
The core method: run every attention in parallel, then see who is missed most

The first step is a single-layer supernetwork: each efficient attention becomes a candidate block, and all of them read the same input side by side. Here the paper borrows a simplification from DARTS — a fixed-α scheme. Instead of learning softmax edge weights or running an expensive bi-level optimization, it simply averages the candidate blocks' outputs: o_bar = (1/N) · Σ o_i over the N candidate blocks. The payoff is a supernetwork that trains all the way to convergence — stable and cheap.

Once it is trained, how do you score each attention? The paper uses a masked validation accuracy drop: mask out one attention block and measure how far validation accuracy falls. The larger the drop, the more that block mattered — the attention whose removal hurts most is judged best for the task. For a homogeneous model, you simply take the top-scoring block and drop it into a full Transformer.

This cheap signal turns out to be surprisingly sharp. On LRA's ListOps task, Reformer earns a masked-validation-drop score of 11.85, while all eight other mechanisms score below 0.5 — a clean, almost unambiguous selection signal. On text classification the search likewise picks out Performer correctly. It is not infallible: on document matching, where the scores are small across the board, the single-layer supernetwork fails to place a true top-3 attention into its own top-3 picks.
Going further: can you search for a mixed-attention model?

Since the supernetwork already holds several attentions together, the natural next thought is to keep more than one and assemble a heterogeneous Transformer. The paper pushes the search space down to the head level — each head is fixed to a single attention type, and the layer averages across heads. Figure 4 contrasts the theoretical version of this idea with the actual implementation, and shows the final form after the search, where every head is set to its optimal attention.

en.caption: Figure 4. The head-level search space. The theoretical version (a) lets each head choose an attention type internally; the actual implementation (b) fixes one attention type per head and averages across heads; (c) is the final multi-head layer after the search, with every head replaced by its optimal attention.

en.text: How do you pull a good mixture out of that space? The paper offers two routes. NAS Prune starts from a multi-head layer where each head carries a different attention, then repeatedly removes the lowest-scoring head and fine-tunes, until only the strongest heads remain (Figure 3). It is accurate but expensive. NAS One-shot skips the iteration entirely: it just takes the four top-scoring attentions from the single-layer selection and stacks them — far cheaper.

en.caption: Figure 3. The NAS Prune procedure. Starting from a four-head layer where each head carries a different attention type, the method repeatedly removes the lowest-scoring head and fine-tunes, until only the strongest heads are left.

en.text: The key result: mixing beats the average, but not the best

The finding splits into two halves that point in opposite directions. The good news: as a way to pick the single best attention, the masked-validation-drop search genuinely works — it gets text classification and ListOps right. The bad news: once the authors assemble those attentions into a heterogeneous Transformer, neither the expensive NAS Prune nor the cheap NAS One-shot beats the best homogeneous model on any of the three tasks.

en.caption: Table 1. Heterogeneous mixed-attention models vs. the best homogeneous model per task (full-model test accuracy, %). On all three tasks, both NAS Prune and NAS One-shot fall short of the best-homogeneous column.
en.note: Numbers from the paper's Table 2. The gap is widest on document matching, where the heterogeneous models trail by roughly 4–6 points.

en.text: A useful practical aside comes from comparing the two search procedures: the expensive NAS Prune (iterative pruning plus fine-tuning) shows no consistent advantage over the cheap NAS One-shot (a single-pass top-four selection) — once the good attentions are correctly identified, the cheap method is enough. Further attempts to tilt the mixture toward the strongest attentions, or give them more heads, produced no consistent gains either.
What to take away

For a new long-range task, instead of training all nine attentions, DARTFormer offers a cheap and reliable recipe: train a single-layer Transformer with the attentions run in parallel, and use masked validation accuracy drop to pick the winner. One caveat: when every candidate's drop score is small (as on document matching), the selection signal can be unreliable and deserves caution.

The more thought-provoking result is the counterintuitive one. Mixing several attention types does beat the average of picking one at random, but it never beats the best single choice. That sits at odds with the common assumption that diverse attention biases add up — at least on these long-range NLP tasks, choosing the right single attention beats blending many. The boundary of the claim is worth stating plainly: it rests on three LRA tasks, nine candidate attentions, and a from-scratch (no-pretraining) setup, and whether it survives other tasks or the addition of pretraining remains open.

zh.text: 自 Transformer 问世以来，研究者为它的自注意力(self-attention)设计了一长串更省算力的替代品：Longformer、Bigbird、Performer、Reformer、Linformer、Synthesizer……原始点积注意力的计算量随序列长度平方增长，这些高效变体正是为了把长序列任务的开销降下来。
问题是：面对一个具体的长序列任务，到底该用哪一种?此前的 Long Range Arena(LRA)基准已经给出一个让人不安的结论——在没有预训练、从零开始训练的设定下，最好的注意力高度依赖任务，没有哪一种能通吃。于是实践者只剩下一条笨办法：把每种注意力都训一遍再挑，代价高得离谱。
这篇 DARTFormer 想把"挑注意力"这件事做得又快又靠谱，同时顺手回答一个长期悬而未决的直觉问题：既然不同的注意力头(attention head)可能各自擅长不同的关系模式，那把多种注意力混在一起，会不会比任何单一注意力都强?论文的做法是把可微架构搜索(DARTS 式的 NAS)搬进 Transformer，先用一个"超网络"把所有候选注意力并联起来，再用一个便宜的打分指标把它们排序。

zh.caption: 图1 DARTFormer 的超网络(左)与搜索得到的最终架构(右)。超网络是一个单层 Transformer，把 Bigbird、Linear、Synthesizer 等多种高效注意力块并联，再对它们的输出取平均;右侧是搜索后导出的模型，在同一层里混合了 Performer 和 Reformer 两种注意力——跨注意力头异构、跨层同构。

zh.text: 论文: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00641
为什么"挑注意力"值得单独研究

在图像领域，卷积核会自动学到不同的特征;类似地，人们长期相信 Transformer 的不同注意力头会学到不同的关系偏置(relational bias)。如果这个直觉成立，那么一个同时容纳多种注意力类型的模型，理应能学到更丰富的关系，从而超过任何单一注意力的模型。DARTFormer 没有把这个直觉当成前提，而是把它当成一个需要被验证的假设，直接去问：一个任务的最优注意力，真的是多种注意力的混合吗?
要回答这个问题，暴力枚举显然行不通——九种注意力、还要考虑它们的各种组合，逐一训练的成本无法承受。这正是把架构搜索引进来的动机：用一次训练同时评估所有候选，而不是训练所有候选。
核心方法：并联所有注意力，再看少了谁最疼

DARTFormer 的第一步是搭一个单层"超网络"：把每一种高效注意力都做成一个候选块(block)，让它们并排接收同样的输入。这里借用了 DARTS 的一个简化技巧——固定 α(fixed-α)：不去学习 softmax 边权重、也不做代价高昂的双层优化(bi-level optimization)，而是直接把所有候选块的输出取平均。公式上就是把 N 个候选块的输出简单平均，o_bar = (1/N)·Σ o_i。好处是这个超网络可以一路训练到收敛，稳定又便宜。
训练好之后，怎么给每种注意力打分?论文用的指标叫"掩码验证精度下降"(masked validation accuracy drop)：把某一个注意力块屏蔽掉，看验证集精度掉多少——掉得越多，说明这个块越重要。删掉谁最疼，谁就是这个任务的最优注意力。对于只想要单一注意力的场景(同构模型)，取得分最高的那一个，放进完整的 Transformer 就行。

这个便宜的打分指标出人意料地灵。以 LRA 的 ListOps 任务为例，Reformer 的掩码验证下降得分高达 11.85，而其余八种注意力全部低于 0.5——这是一个干净利落、几乎没有歧义的选择信号。在文本分类任务上，搜索同样正确地把 Performer 选了出来。当然它并非万能：在得分整体偏小的文档匹配(document matching)任务上，单层超网络就没能把真正的前三名稳定选进自己的前三。
更进一步：能不能搜出一个"混合注意力"的模型
既然超网络天生就把多种注意力放在一起，很自然会想：干脆保留多种、拼成一个异构(heterogeneous)Transformer，会不会更强?论文把搜索空间下沉到注意力头这一层——让每个头固定使用一种注意力，整层再对各头的输出取平均。图4 对比了这个想法的"理论版"和"实际实现版"，以及搜索结束后每个头都换成最优注意力的最终形态。

zh.caption: 图4 注意力头层面的搜索空间。理论版(a)让每个头内部再去挑注意力类型;实际实现(b)改为每个头固定一种注意力、整层对各头输出取平均;(c)是搜索完成后每个头都替换为"最优注意力"的最终多头注意力层。

zh.text: 怎么从这个空间里挑出好的混合?论文给了两条路。一条叫 NAS Prune：从一个每个头都装着不同注意力的多头层出发，反复删掉得分最低的那个头、再微调，直到只剩下表现最好的若干头(图3)。这条路准确但昂贵。另一条叫 NAS One-shot：干脆不迭代，直接从单层选择里取得分最高的四种注意力拼起来——便宜得多。

zh.caption: 图3 NAS Prune 的迭代剪枝过程：从一个四头、每头装有不同注意力的混合层出发，反复删掉得分最低的注意力头并微调，直到只留下最强的几个头。

zh.text: 关键结果：混合能赢过"平均"，但赢不过"最好"
结论分成方向相反的两半。好消息是，掩码验证下降这个搜索指标在挑"单一最优注意力"上是真的好用——文本分类和 ListOps 上它都选对了。坏消息是，当作者把多种注意力拼成异构 Transformer 后，无论用昂贵的 NAS Prune 还是便宜的 NAS One-shot，在全部三个任务上都没能超过最好的那个同构模型。

zh.caption: 表1 异构混合注意力模型 vs. 各任务上最优的同构模型(完整模型的测试精度 %)。三个任务上，NAS Prune 和 NAS One-shot 都没有超过"最优同构"这一列。
zh.note: 数据来自论文 Table 2。文档匹配任务上差距最大，异构模型落后约 4–6 个百分点。

zh.text: 一个有用的实践旁证来自两种搜索方法的对比：昂贵的 NAS Prune(反复剪枝加微调)相对便宜的 NAS One-shot(单遍取前四)并没有稳定的优势——只要好的注意力被正确识别出来，便宜的方法就够用了。作者进一步尝试把混合向最强的注意力倾斜、或给强注意力分配更多头，同样没能带来一致的提升。
这告诉我们什么
对一个新的长序列任务，与其把九种注意力全训一遍，DARTFormer 给了一条便宜可靠的配方：训练一个单层、多注意力并联的 Transformer，用掩码验证精度下降来挑赢家。一个提醒是：如果所有候选的下降得分都很小(比如文档匹配那种量级)，这个选择信号就可能不可靠，需要谨慎。

更值得回味的是那个反直觉的结论。混合多种注意力，确实能打败"随便挑一个"的平均水平，却始终打不过"挑得最好"的那一个。这与"不同注意力偏置会互补叠加"的常见假设相冲突——至少在这些长序列 NLP 任务上，与其把多种注意力揉在一起，不如踏踏实实为任务选对那一种。当然，论文的边界也很清楚：结论建立在 LRA 的三个任务、九种候选注意力、从零训练(无预训练)的设定之上，换到别的任务或引入预训练后是否依旧成立，仍是开放问题。

DARTFormer 的第一步是搭一个单层"超网络"：把每一种高效注意力都做成一个候选块(block)，让它们并排接收同样的输入。这里借用了 DARTS 的一个简化技巧——固定 α(fixed-α)：不去学习 softmax 边权重、也不做代价高昂的双层优化(bi-level optimization)，而是直接把所有候选块的输出取平均。公式上就是把 N 个候选块的输出简单平均，o_bar = (1/N)·Σ o_i。好处是这个超网络可以一路训练到收敛，稳定又便宜。
训练好之后，怎么给每种注意力打分?论文用的指标叫"掩码验证精度下降"(masked validation accuracy drop)：把某一个注意力块屏蔽掉，看验证集精度掉多少——掉得越多，说明这个块越重要。删掉谁最疼，谁就是这个任务的最优注意力。对于只想要单一注意力的场景(同构模型)，取得分最高的那一个，放进完整的 Transformer 就行。

这个便宜的打分指标出人意料地灵。以 LRA 的 ListOps 任务为例，Reformer 的掩码验证下降得分高达 11.85，而其余八种注意力全部低于 0.5——这是一个干净利落、几乎没有歧义的选择信号。在文本分类任务上，搜索同样正确地把 Performer 选了出来。当然它并非万能：在得分整体偏小的文档匹配(document matching)任务上，单层超网络就没能把真正的前三名稳定选进自己的前三。

en.caption: Figure 4. The head-level search space. The theoretical version (a) lets each head choose an attention type internally; the actual implementation (b) fixes one attention type per head and averages across heads; (c) is the final multi-head layer after the search, with every head replaced by its optimal attention.

en.text: Why picking an attention deserves its own method

In vision, convolutional kernels learn different features on their own, and there is a long-standing belief that a Transformer's attention heads similarly learn different relational biases. If that holds, a model that hosts several attention types at once ought to capture a richer set of relationships and outperform any single-attention model. Rather than assume this, DARTFormer treats it as a hypothesis to test and asks it directly: is the optimal attention for a task actually a mixture of several attentions?

Answering that by brute force is a non-starter — nine candidate mechanisms, plus their combinations, is far too much to train one at a time. That is the motivation for a search: evaluate every candidate in a single training run instead of training every candidate.
The core method: run every attention in parallel, then see who is missed most

The first step is a single-layer supernetwork: each efficient attention becomes a candidate block, and all of them read the same input side by side. Here the paper borrows a simplification from DARTS — a fixed-α scheme. Instead of learning softmax edge weights or running an expensive bi-level optimization, it simply averages the candidate blocks' outputs: o_bar = (1/N) · Σ o_i over the N candidate blocks. The payoff is a supernetwork that trains all the way to convergence — stable and cheap.

Once it is trained, how do you score each attention? The paper uses a masked validation accuracy drop: mask out one attention block and measure how far validation accuracy falls. The larger the drop, the more that block mattered — the attention whose removal hurts most is judged best for the task. For a homogeneous model, you simply take the top-scoring block and drop it into a full Transformer.

This cheap signal turns out to be surprisingly sharp. On LRA's ListOps task, Reformer earns a masked-validation-drop score of 11.85, while all eight other mechanisms score below 0.5 — a clean, almost unambiguous selection signal. On text classification the search likewise picks out Performer correctly. It is not infallible: on document matching, where the scores are small across the board, the single-layer supernetwork fails to place a true top-3 attention into its own top-3 picks.

en.subtitle: DARTFormer, from Cambridge, Imperial, and Oxford, brings differentiable architecture search to attention selection — and tests whether mixing several attention types beats picking the best single one.

zh.title: 注意力机制那么多，到底该选哪个?
zh.subtitle: 剑桥、帝国理工与牛津提出 DARTFormer：用可微架构搜索为长序列任务挑注意力，并回答了一个更尖锐的问题——混合多种注意力会更好吗?

en.text: Ever since the Transformer arrived, researchers have produced a long menu of cheaper stand-ins for its self-attention: Longformer, Bigbird, Performer, Reformer, Linformer, Synthesizer, and more. The original dot-product attention scales quadratically with sequence length, and these efficient variants exist to cut that cost on long-sequence tasks.

The awkward part is choosing one. For a given long-range task, which efficient attention should you reach for? Earlier work on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark delivered an uncomfortable answer: when models are trained from scratch, with no pretraining, the best attention depends heavily on the task, and none of them wins everywhere. That leaves practitioners with a brute-force fallback — train every attention and compare — which is absurdly expensive.

DARTFormer sets out to make attention selection both cheap and reliable, and along the way it takes on a question the field has left hanging: since different attention heads may specialize in different kinds of relationships, would a model that mixes several attention types beat any single one? The paper adapts differentiable architecture search (DARTS-style NAS) to the Transformer. It builds a supernetwork that runs every candidate attention in parallel, then ranks them with a cheap scoring signal.

The supernetwork is a single-layer Transformer that runs many efficient attention blocks — Bigbird, Linear, Synthesizer, and others — in parallel and averages their outputs. The derived model on the right mixes two attention types, Performer and Reformer, inside one layer: heterogeneous across heads, homogeneous across layers.

zh.text: 自 Transformer 问世以来，研究者为它的自注意力(self-attention)设计了一长串更省算力的替代品：Longformer、Bigbird、Performer、Reformer、Linformer、Synthesizer……原始点积注意力的计算量随序列长度平方增长，这些高效变体正是为了把长序列任务的开销降下来。
问题是：面对一个具体的长序列任务，到底该用哪一种?此前的 Long Range Arena(LRA)基准已经给出一个让人不安的结论——在没有预训练、从零开始训练的设定下，最好的注意力高度依赖任务，没有哪一种能通吃。于是实践者只剩下一条笨办法：把每种注意力都训一遍再挑，代价高得离谱。
这篇 DARTFormer 想把"挑注意力"这件事做得又快又靠谱，同时顺手回答一个长期悬而未决的直觉问题：既然不同的注意力头(attention head)可能各自擅长不同的关系模式，那把多种注意力混在一起，会不会比任何单一注意力都强?论文的做法是把可微架构搜索(DARTS 式的 NAS)搬进 Transformer，先用一个"超网络"把所有候选注意力并联起来，再用一个便宜的打分指标把它们排序。

zh.title: 注意力机制那么多，到底该选哪个?

en.text: The key result: mixing beats the average, but not the best

The finding splits into two halves that point in opposite directions. The good news: as a way to pick the single best attention, the masked-validation-drop search genuinely works — it gets text classification and ListOps right. The bad news: once the authors assemble those attentions into a heterogeneous Transformer, neither the expensive NAS Prune nor the cheap NAS One-shot beats the best homogeneous model on any of the three tasks.

en.text: A useful practical aside comes from comparing the two search procedures: the expensive NAS Prune (iterative pruning plus fine-tuning) shows no consistent advantage over the cheap NAS One-shot (a single-pass top-four selection) — once the good attentions are correctly identified, the cheap method is enough. Further attempts to tilt the mixture toward the strongest attentions, or give them more heads, produced no consistent gains either.
What to take away

For a new long-range task, instead of training all nine attentions, DARTFormer offers a cheap and reliable recipe: train a single-layer Transformer with the attentions run in parallel, and use masked validation accuracy drop to pick the winner. One caveat: when every candidate's drop score is small (as on document matching), the selection signal can be unreliable and deserves caution.

The more thought-provoking result is the counterintuitive one. Mixing several attention types does beat the average of picking one at random, but it never beats the best single choice. That sits at odds with the common assumption that diverse attention biases add up — at least on these long-range NLP tasks, choosing the right single attention beats blending many. The boundary of the claim is worth stating plainly: it rests on three LRA tasks, nine candidate attentions, and a from-scratch (no-pretraining) setup, and whether it survives other tasks or the addition of pretraining remains open.

zh.text: 这告诉我们什么
对一个新的长序列任务，与其把九种注意力全训一遍，DARTFormer 给了一条便宜可靠的配方：训练一个单层、多注意力并联的 Transformer，用掩码验证精度下降来挑赢家。一个提醒是：如果所有候选的下降得分都很小(比如文档匹配那种量级)，这个选择信号就可能不可靠，需要谨慎。

更值得回味的是那个反直觉的结论。混合多种注意力，确实能打败"随便挑一个"的平均水平，却始终打不过"挑得最好"的那一个。这与"不同注意力偏置会互补叠加"的常见假设相冲突——至少在这些长序列 NLP 任务上，与其把多种注意力揉在一起，不如踏踏实实为任务选对那一种。当然，论文的边界也很清楚：结论建立在 LRA 的三个任务、九种候选注意力、从零训练(无预训练)的设定之上，换到别的任务或引入预训练后是否依旧成立，仍是开放问题。

对一个新的长序列任务，与其把九种注意力全训一遍，DARTFormer 给了一条便宜可靠的配方：训练一个单层、多注意力并联的 Transformer，用掩码验证精度下降来挑赢家。一个提醒是：如果所有候选的下降得分都很小(比如文档匹配那种量级)，这个选择信号就可能不可靠，需要谨慎。

更值得回味的是那个反直觉的结论。混合多种注意力，确实能打败"随便挑一个"的平均水平，却始终打不过"挑得最好"的那一个。这与"不同注意力偏置会互补叠加"的常见假设相冲突——至少在这些长序列 NLP 任务上，与其把多种注意力揉在一起，不如踏踏实实为任务选对那一种。当然，论文的边界也很清楚：结论建立在 LRA 的三个任务、九种候选注意力、从零训练(无预训练)的设定之上，换到别的任务或引入预训练后是否依旧成立，仍是开放问题。

en.title: So Many Attention Mechanisms — Which One Should You Actually Use?
en.subtitle: DARTFormer, from Cambridge, Imperial, and Oxford, brings differentiable architecture search to attention selection — and tests whether mixing several attention types beats picking the best single one.

zh.title: 注意力机制那么多，到底该选哪个?
zh.subtitle: 剑桥、帝国理工与牛津提出 DARTFormer：用可微架构搜索为长序列任务挑注意力，并回答了一个更尖锐的问题——混合多种注意力会更好吗?

en.caption: Figure 1. The DARTFormer supernetwork (left) and a derived final architecture (right). The supernetwork is a single-layer Transformer that runs many efficient attention blocks — Bigbird, Linear, Synthesizer, and others — in parallel and averages their outputs. The derived model on the right mixes two attention types, Performer and Reformer, inside one layer: heterogeneous across heads, homogeneous across layers.

en.text: What to take away

For a new long-range task, instead of training all nine attentions, DARTFormer offers a cheap and reliable recipe: train a single-layer Transformer with the attentions run in parallel, and use masked validation accuracy drop to pick the winner. One caveat: when every candidate's drop score is small (as on document matching), the selection signal can be unreliable and deserves caution.

The more thought-provoking result is the counterintuitive one. Mixing several attention types does beat the average of picking one at random, but it never beats the best single choice. That sits at odds with the common assumption that diverse attention biases add up — at least on these long-range NLP tasks, choosing the right single attention beats blending many. The boundary of the claim is worth stating plainly: it rests on three LRA tasks, nine candidate attentions, and a from-scratch (no-pretraining) setup, and whether it survives other tasks or the addition of pretraining remains open.

zh.text: 自 Transformer 问世以来，研究者为它的自注意力(self-attention)设计了一长串更省算力的替代品：Longformer、Bigbird、Performer、Reformer、Linformer、Synthesizer……原始点积注意力的计算量随序列长度平方增长，这些高效变体正是为了把长序列任务的开销降下来。
问题是：面对一个具体的长序列任务，到底该用哪一种?此前的 Long Range Arena(LRA)基准已经给出一个让人不安的结论——在没有预训练、从零开始训练的设定下，最好的注意力高度依赖任务，没有哪一种能通吃。于是实践者只剩下一条笨办法：把每种注意力都训一遍再挑，代价高得离谱。
这篇 DARTFormer 想把"挑注意力"这件事做得又快又靠谱，同时顺手回答一个长期悬而未决的直觉问题：既然不同的注意力头(attention head)可能各自擅长不同的关系模式，那把多种注意力混在一起，会不会比任何单一注意力都强?论文的做法是把可微架构搜索(DARTS 式的 NAS)搬进 Transformer，先用一个"超网络"把所有候选注意力并联起来，再用一个便宜的打分指标把它们排序。

zh.caption: 图1 DARTFormer 的超网络(左)与搜索得到的最终架构(右)。超网络是一个单层 Transformer，把 Bigbird、Linear、Synthesizer 等多种高效注意力块并联，再对它们的输出取平均;右侧是搜索后导出的模型，在同一层里混合了 Performer 和 Reformer 两种注意力——跨注意力头异构、跨层同构。

zh.text: 论文: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00641
关键结果：混合能赢过"平均"，但赢不过"最好"
结论分成方向相反的两半。好消息是，掩码验证下降这个搜索指标在挑"单一最优注意力"上是真的好用——文本分类和 ListOps 上它都选对了。坏消息是，当作者把多种注意力拼成异构 Transformer 后，无论用昂贵的 NAS Prune 还是便宜的 NAS One-shot，在全部三个任务上都没能超过最好的那个同构模型。

zh.caption: 表1 异构混合注意力模型 vs. 各任务上最优的同构模型(完整模型的测试精度 %)。三个任务上，NAS Prune 和 NAS One-shot 都没有超过"最优同构"这一列。
zh.note: 数据来自论文 Table 2。文档匹配任务上差距最大，异构模型落后约 4–6 个百分点。

zh.text: 一个有用的实践旁证来自两种搜索方法的对比：昂贵的 NAS Prune(反复剪枝加微调)相对便宜的 NAS One-shot(单遍取前四)并没有稳定的优势——只要好的注意力被正确识别出来，便宜的方法就够用了。作者进一步尝试把混合向最强的注意力倾斜、或给强注意力分配更多头，同样没能带来一致的提升。
